name: Fibo 2.0 Edit
author: michaeldune
description: Bria's Fibo 2.0 Edit Turbo: hand it a picture and a sentence, and it changes the one thing you named. Eight steps, about 14 seconds for a 1 megapixel picture on a 12 GB card. In a side-by-side against MOSS-Image Edit on the same pictures, instructions and seeds it was the better editor: told to make a red bicycle yellow it recoloured that bicycle, same frame and same fenders, where MOSS drew a different bicycle; told to repaint a shop front and keep the signs it kept them; and it holds faces, skin tone and the original light closer. Lettering in the picture survives either way. Where it is weaker: a heavy style change (photo to watercolour) drifts the face more than MOSS does. A ratio that does not match your picture centre-crops it, but unlike the MOSS edit card the edit itself still holds up, lettering included. LICENCE: the Fibo 2.0 weights are CC BY-NC 4.0, NON-COMMERCIAL USE ONLY. Selling the pictures, or using them in anything commercial, needs a separate agreement with BRIA AI (platform.bria.ai/licensing). 13.3 GB download. Needs a SimpliGen engine with native Fibo 2.0 support, which landed in ComfyUI on 21 October, after the v0.42.1 tag.

presets.name: Fibo 2.0 Edit
presets.description: Give it a picture and a sentence. Name the change and name what to keep: "Change only the red bicycle to a bright yellow bicycle. Keep everything else in the street exactly as it is." Colour, outfit, lighting, season and weather changes hold the rest of the frame in place, text in the picture comes through letter-exact, and an object you recolour stays the same object. Pick the ratio that matches your picture to keep the whole frame; another ratio just crops it. Non-commercial use only — see the pack description.

requirements.notes: Weights: Comfy-Org/Fibo-2.0 pinned to commit b2bffaf5 - Fibo 2.0 Edit Turbo int8 ConvRot (8.41 GB) and the Qwen3-VL 4B text encoder in int8 ConvRot (4.86 GB, NOT the 8B) - plus the Flux 2 autoencoder already used by the MOSS and Flux 2 packs. Both Fibo files verified against the Hugging Face X-Linked-ETag; sha256 pinned in the pack checksums. LICENCE: Fibo 2.0 weights are (c) BRIA AI under CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial only; commercial use needs an agreement with BRIA (platform.bria.ai/licensing). Qwen3-VL and the Flux 2 VAE are not restricted that way. Graph: core nodes only besides rgthree; CLIPLoader type fibo2, TextEncodeFibo2 (it emits the latent itself and centre-crops the reference internally, so there is no EmptyLatent and no ImageScale node), KSampler euler/simple at 8 steps CFG 1; no Skip Layer Guidance (untested on this model). NEEDS a ComfyUI at or after 87ed5a06 (2026-10-21, PR 17240), which is NOT in any tagged release as of 2026-10-23 (newest tag v0.42.1, 10-19); minComfyuiVersion is set to v0.43.0 on the ASSUMPTION that the next tag carries it, which is unverified - confirm the real gate before release. TESTED 2026-10-23 engine-direct on a 4070 Ti 12 GB, vanilla ComfyUI fb3befd1: 18 arms over 3 sources x 3 instruction types x 2 seeds, a 4-vs-8 step sweep and a prompt-tagging arm, about 14 s per 1 MP picture at 8 steps (10-12 s at 4). Run head to head against the moss-image-edit pack on identical inputs: Fibo recoloured a bicycle keeping its frame and fenders where MOSS drew a different bicycle and on one seed invented a basket; it kept a chalkboard frame that MOSS repainted; face MAD against the source 4.4 vs 8.6 on a dress recolour and 26.0 vs 40.3 on a golden-hour relight; mean keep-region MAD 32.16 vs 41.92. Lettering came through letter-exact in 12 of 12 shopfront arms on both models. Known: a heavy style change (photo to watercolour) drifts the face further than MOSS does; 8 steps is marginally cleaner than 4 in letterforms; naming the reference as <image_1> in the prompt made no measurable difference on a single-picture edit. This pack file's own workflow was then run through the app's substitution rules on the same engine at two aspect ratios: 1184x896 (matches the source) in 20 s and 1024x1024 (centre-crops) in 12 s, and unlike the moss-image-edit card the mismatched ratio did NOT degrade the edit - navy paintwork, wooden sign board kept and both signs still letter-exact. Reported by two tutorials but NOT measured here: Fibo renders Latin script only, failing Chinese and Hindi signs where MOSS succeeds. 1.0.1 drops the app's sdxl-template prompt suffix with values.quality, for the same reason as the moss-image-edit card, where it caused a visible fault; on this card the suffix changed little (mean abs difference 0.70, no visible fault), but with it removed the in-app render is bit-identical to the engine-direct bake. VERIFIED IN-APP 2026-10-27 on ComfyUI v0.43.0. PREVIOUSLY NOT TESTED: this pack file inside the app (the engine does not have the nodes yet), the rgthree user-LoRA marker on this graph (vanilla has no rgthree, so it was bypassed for the engine run), multi-reference editing (the node takes up to 16 pictures), Fibo 2.0 Dev, and VGL structured-JSON prompting.
